title: Establish eval scorecards and auto-rollback heuristics for rollouts
creator: Priya Patel
description:
Goal: Build a production-ready evaluation scorecard service and integrate it into the rollout orchestration layer so that canary rollouts, A/B experiments, and shadow traffic pipelines are gated by automated quality checks and can auto-trigger rollback when regressions are detected.

Scope and acceptance criteria:
- Define a small, extensible scorecard schema for per-model/per-route evaluation that supports: golden prompt sets, metric definitions (semantic-similarity, correctness, hallucination rate, safety flags, latency percentiles), and aggregation windows.
- Implement a realtime scoring pipeline that can score shadowed responses and snippet responses from live traffic within the canary window.
- Add gating rules to the rollout orchestrator: configurable thresholds (absolute + relative delta) and multi-metric policies (e.g., fail if any critical metric drops by >3% AND absolute value < threshold).
- Implement auto-rollback action triggered by sustained regression for the configured evaluation window (e.g., 30m with 5% margin). Rollback must include a clear audit event and notification to on-call and owning team.
- Expose a scorecard dashboard (per-rollout, per-customer where applicable) and a historical view of eval metrics to support post-mortem and tuning.

Design decisions and trade-offs considered: 
- Live scoring vs periodic offline evaluation: We prioritize live scoring for shadow traffic to catch regressions that only appear on production distributions; heavy compute evals remain offline.
- Metric selection: Use a hybrid of embedding-similarity (cosine to reference outputs), model-internal perplexity delta for unexpected token distribution shifts, deterministic golden-answer checks where feasible, and domain-specific safety flags. This balances sensitivity and actionable signal.
- Thresholding strategy: Support both absolute thresholds and relative delta thresholds (percent change vs baseline) to catch dropouts during model upgrades but avoid false positives for low-traffic slices.
- Per-customer gating: Provide opt-in gating for Dedicated/Private customers (different baselines and golden sets). Hosted customers use global canonical golden sets unless they supply their own.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Spec the scorecard schema and canonical golden prompt sets (Confluence doc: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b-eval-spec).
2) Implement scoring microservice and proto for result emission (ENG-8021 does infra plumbing).
3) Hook scoring into shadow traffic path and A/B runner (add sampling and response capture).
4) Implement gating rules in rollout orchestrator with durable audit events and rollback API.
5) Dashboards + alerts (Grafana/Tempo links in comments).
6) Run staged canaries to validate thresholds (start with non-critical routes).

Open questions / risks:
- Label noise on golden datasets leading to false alarms; need tooling to update golden sets and mark problematic prompts.
- Cost: live scoring increases compute; need batching and sampling policies to manage cost.
- Latency constraints for scoring: we will run scoring asynchronously for shadow traffic; critical path rollouts still depend on aggregated metrics, not per-request latency.

Files and artifacts: 
- Spec PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/146
- Scoring library spike: https://github.com/redwood-inference/scorecards/tree/spike
- Dashboard prototype: https://grafana.internal.redwood/board/rollout-scorecards

How this ties to product requirements: PM asks for guarded rollouts to prevent quality regressions visible in production traffic. This implementation will give us automated safety nets for faster rollouts while reducing manual QA burden.

Next milestones (priority ordering):
- Finish scorecard schema and golden set curation (owner: Priya) — target 2026-03-05.
- Deliver scoring service MVP and shadow integration (owner: Miguel) — target 2026-03-18.
- Rollout gating integration and auto-rollback with e2e tests (owner: Miguel + infra) — target 2026-03-31.
